rationale: Because market cap dominates three years of capex for the vast majority of firms, this is numerically almost identical to plain sales-to-price (a classic published value anomaly) and structurally the same "add a capital stock to the market-value denominator" trick already tested as CapitalAdjustedEbitdaYield in the archive.

The conjunction of earnings yield with a within-firm trend in sales-per-unit-of-net-PPE is a coherent and reasonably novel "cheap plus improving capital productivity" construct not yet in the archive, though the trend leg can be mechanically driven by PPE shrinkage and thus partially proxy the known low-investment effect.

This is the same "expensive multiple × rising investment intensity" template already tested twice in the archive (PriceyGoodwillRollup, PriceyInventoryOverbuild), with only the investment proxy and the RANK→IND_RANK wrapper changed, so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

Direct rediscovery of the archived PriceyInventoryOverbuild — same MIN gate, same price-to-revenue leg, same inventory-intensity leg with DELTA swapped for TS_RANK and RANK swapped for IND_RANK — which is precisely the kind of cosmetic re-specification the objective warns against.

This is essentially the sign-mirrored twin of the archived PriceyGoodwillRollup (valuation crossed with intangible/goodwill accumulation), and the second leg is weakened by the fact that a falling intan/at often reflects routine amortization or asset-base growth rather than any deliberate restraint in intangible investment.

It overlaps the archived SalesValueHiringDiscipline and the published labor-hiring anomaly, but the employment-minus-sales growth gap is a genuinely different construct (deteriorating labor productivity rather than raw headcount growth) and the product-of-ranks orientation is internally consistent with the negative expected sign.
